aspects.says: DebugFilter puts the image a channel read next to the unpacked message, and the image shows the card number unmasked.
basis: section:17.4 Each View of the Bytes Answers a Different Question

aspects.says: A dump from outside is evidence only when it reads back to the bytes it shows: decodeHexDump reads one layout and checks nothing, so a reader checks each line's offset and reads bytes from their columns.
basis: section:17.1 A Dump Is Evidence Only When It Reads Back to the Bytes It Shows

aspects.says: Two messages are compared field by field in field order, without the bitmap, binary values by content and nested fields sub-field by sub-field.
basis: section:17.3 Two Messages Are Compared Field by Field, and Binary Fields by Content

aspects.says: FlatLogListener passes on a frozen text event with no message and no realm, so masking and realm filters must come before it.
basis: section:17.6.1 Spot the Problem: One Line per Event

aspects.says: A message read back from a protected log packs to the sent bytes only after its packager is set and every masked or wiped field gets a test value; a masked card number packs silently into different bytes.
basis: section:17.2 A Logged Message Gives Back the Bytes Only After You Put Back What the Log Masked

aspects.says: zeropad(long) keeps the last digits silently, protect masks the whole track after the separator, and bitSet2String starts at bit 0.
basis: section:17.5 ISOUtil's Helpers Fail Quietly Where You Expect an Error

aspects.says: A failed unpack and DebugFilter put raw bytes into the event as entries the masking filter can't see, and a listener of your own replaces those entries, leaves messages alone and returns the event.
basis: section:17.6 Raw Bytes in the Log Are Text, So a Filter of Your Own Has to Withhold Them

aspects.says: hexString, dumpString, hexdump and hexDump with a character set answer different questions about the same bytes.
basis: section:17.4 Each View of the Bytes Answers a Different Question
aspects.reason: choosing a view is a reading skill on library output; nothing the reader writes would differ in a graded run
